```{r}
#Calculate the number of missing values of the city.
#You should use the data in the file "house_sales.csv".
#Your output should be an object missing_city, that contains the number of missing values in this column.

#Use this cell to write your code for Task 1
#install.packages("randomForest")
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
house <- read_csv(here('Data', 'house_sales.csv'))
missing_city <- sum(is.na(house$city) | house$city == "--")
missing_city
```

```{r}
#Before you fit any models, you will need to make sure the data is clean.
#The table below shows what the data should look like.
#Create a cleaned version of the dataframe.
#You should start with the data in the file "house_sales.csv".
#Your output should be a dataframe named clean_data.
#All column names and values should match the table below.

#Use this cell to write your code for Task 2
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
house<-read_csv(here('Data', 'house_sales.csv'))
house
str(house)
clean_data<-house%>%
filter(!is.na(sale_price))%>%
mutate(city=ifelse(is.na(city),"Unknown", city), city=ifelse(city=="--", "Unknown", city))%>%
mutate(months_listed=ifelse(is.na(months_listed), round(mean(months_listed, na.rm=TRUE), 1), months_listed))%>%
mutate(bedrooms=ifelse(is.na(bedrooms), round(mean(bedrooms, na.rm=TRUE)), bedrooms))%>%
mutate(house_type = case_when(
    str_detect(house_type, "^Terr") ~ "Terraced",
    str_detect(house_type, "^Semi") ~ "Semi-detached",
    str_detect(house_type, "^Det") ~ "Detached",
    TRUE ~ house_type)) %>%
mutate(house_type = ifelse(is.na(house_type),names(sort(table(house_type), decreasing = TRUE))[1],house_type)) %>%
mutate(area=as.numeric(str_replace(area, " sq.m.", "")), area=ifelse(is.na(area), round(mean(area, na.rm=TRUE), 1), area))
clean_data
```

```{r}
#The team at RealAgents have told you that they have always believed that the number of bedrooms is the biggest driver of house price.
#Producing a table showing the difference in the average sale price by number of bedrooms along with the variance to investigate this question for the team.
#You should start with the data in the file 'house_sales.csv'.
#Your output should be a data frame named price_by_rooms.
#It should include the three columns bedrooms, avg_price, var_price.
#Your answers should be rounded to 1 decimal place.

#Use this cell to write your code for Task 3
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
house <- read_csv(here('Data', 'house_sales.csv'))
price_by_rooms<-house %>%
filter(!is.na(sale_price))%>%
group_by(bedrooms)%>%
summarize(avg_price = round(mean(sale_price), 1), var_price = round(var(sale_price), 1), .groups = 'drop') %>%
arrange(bedrooms)
price_by_rooms
```

```{r}
#Fit a baseline model to predict the sale price of a house.
#Fit your model using the data contained in “train.csv”
#Use “validation.csv” to predict new values based on your model. You must return a dataframe named base_result, that includes house_id and price. The price column must be your predicted values

#Use this cell to write your code for Task 4
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
train <- read_csv(here('data', 'train.csv'))
validation <- read_csv(here('data', 'validation.csv'))
#City mapping (label encoding)
city_mapping <- c('Teasdale' = 0, 'Silvertown' = 1, 'Poppleton' = 2, 'Riverford' = 3)
house_type_mapping <- c('Detached' = 0, 'Semi-detached' = 1, 'Terraced' = 2)
train <- train %>%
mutate(city = recode(city, !!!city_mapping),
  house_type = recode(house_type, !!!house_type_mapping))
validation <- validation %>%
mutate(city = recode(city, !!!city_mapping),
  house_type = recode(house_type, !!!house_type_mapping))
#Date features
train <- train %>%
mutate(sale_date = as.Date(sale_date),
  day = day(sale_date),
  month = month(sale_date),
  year = year(sale_date))
validation <- validation %>%
mutate(sale_date = as.Date(sale_date),
  day = day(sale_date),
  month = month(sale_date),
  year = year(sale_date))
# Prepare features (drop house_id, sale_price, sale_date)
X_train <- train %>% select(-house_id, -sale_price, -sale_date)
y_train <- train$sale_price
X_validation <- validation %>% select(-house_id, -sale_date)
# Build training data frame with sale_price included
train_df <- cbind(sale_price = y_train, X_train)
# Linear Regression (Task 4 - baseline model)
baseline_model <- lm(sale_price ~ ., data = train_df)
# Predict on validation set
validation$price <- predict(baseline_model, newdata = X_validation)
# Final result
base_result <- validation %>%
select(house_id, price) %>%
mutate(price = round(price, 1))
base_result
# Direct from model residuals
rmse_baseline <- sqrt(mean(baseline_model$residuals^2))
rmse_baseline
```

```{r}
#Fit a comparison model to predict the sale price of a house.
#Fit your model using the data contained in “train.csv”
#Use “validation.csv” to predict new values based on your model. You must return a dataframe named compare_result, that includes house_id and price. The price column must be your predicted values.

#Use this cell to write your code for Task 5
library(randomForest)
train_df <- cbind(sale_price = y_train, X_train)
#Fit Random Forest comparison model
comparison_model <- randomForest(sale_price ~ ., data = train_df)
#Predict on validation set
validation$price <- predict(comparison_model, newdata = X_validation)
#Final result
compare_result <- validation %>%
select(house_id, price) %>%
mutate(price = round(price, 1))
compare_result
#Training RMSE for comparison model
train_pred_rf <- predict(comparison_model)
rmse_comparison <- sqrt(mean((y_train - train_pred_rf)^2))
cat("Comparison Model (RF) Training RMSE:", round(rmse_comparison, 0), "\n")
#Compare with baseline
cat("Baseline (LM) Training RMSE: 21536\n")
cat("Improvement:", round(21536 - rmse_comparison, 0), "points\n")
```
